instructions: The night before, or at least 4 hours ahead: sift the cocoa powder into a medium bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 tsp salt and whisk slowly. It looks dry at first, then comes together into a thick, fudgy paste.
Whisk in a few splashes of the milk until it's smooth, then whisk in the rest of the milk.
Whisk in the 1/2 cup Greek yogurt until there are no streaks left.
Whisk in the 1/2 cup chia seeds. Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge.
After about 30 minutes, whisk it once more so the seeds don't settle in clumps.
Covered, it keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. In the morning, stir it, spoon it into bowls and top with the raspberries.
advance_prep_notes: Mix the pudding the night before (at least 4 hours ahead).
method_notes: All three stir chia seeds and cocoa into milk with maple syrup and leave it in the fridge until it sets. Well Plated (the lead) makes a cocoa paste with the syrup first, so it never goes lumpy, and adds Greek yogurt for a creamier, richer pudding. Flavor the Moments and Chocolate Covered Katie leave out the yogurt and use about a quarter cup of chia per cup of milk. This one follows the lead for four, without its optional espresso powder, with raspberries on top.
